pillars.title: Three pillars, one reliability score
pillars.subtitle: SandorHii combines three complementary angles of analysis to verify content. What sets us apart: the linguistic pillar — it dissects how a text tries to manipulate, not just what it shows.

linguistic.label: Linguistic analysis
linguistic.description: Fallacies, alarmist vocabulary, suspicious repetition: every manipulation technique is detected and explained, sentence by sentence.

media.label: Media analysis
media.description: Reverse image and video search, source credibility, tracing how content spreads.

tech.label: Technical analysis
tech.description: Deepfake detection, AI-generated content, and coordinated inauthentic distribution networks.

faux_dilemme.label: False dilemma
faux_dilemme.explanation: The text presents two options as if they were the only ones possible, when others almost always exist.

pente_glissante.label: Slippery slope
pente_glissante.explanation: The text claims a first action will inevitably trigger a chain of extreme consequences, without demonstrating it.

generalisation_abusive.label: Hasty generalization
generalisation_abusive.explanation: A general conclusion is drawn from one or two examples, or an entire group is described with 'all'/'none'/'never'.

ad_hominem.label: Personal attack (ad hominem)
ad_hominem.explanation: The text attacks the person (their character, their morality) instead of discussing their arguments.

autorite_vague.label: Appeal to an unnamed authority
autorite_vague.explanation: The text invokes "experts" or "scientists" without ever naming them or citing a verifiable source.

complot.label: Conspiratorial language
complot.explanation: The text suggests a truth deliberately hidden by "them", without presenting verifiable evidence.

detournement_whataboutism.label: Deflection ("what about them?")
detournement_whataboutism.explanation: Instead of addressing the substance, the text redirects attention to another topic or actor, without addressing the original accusation.

homme_de_paille.label: Straw man (likely)
homme_de_paille.explanation: The text restates an opponent's position in a caricatured way before refuting it — check it against the original source.

urgence_partage.label: Urgency to share
urgence_partage.explanation: The text pushes you to share or act immediately, before reflecting — a classic rapid-spread technique.

urgence_lexicale.label: Urgency vocabulary
urgence_lexicale.explanation: Immediate-alert wording ("urgent", "alert") used to short-circuit verification.

superlatifs.label: Excessive superlatives
superlatifs.explanation: Extreme phrasing ("never seen before", "unprecedented") that exaggerates the scale of a fact to strike the imagination.

mots_choc.label: Shock words
mots_choc.explanation: Vocabulary chosen to provoke a strong emotional reaction rather than to inform.

appel_emotion_peur.label: Appeal to emotion (fear)
appel_emotion_peur.explanation: The text seeks to frighten rather than inform about the facts.

majuscules_excessives.label: Excessive use of capital letters
majuscules_excessives.explanation: An unusually high share of the text is written IN CAPITAL LETTERS, a technique used to simulate urgency or authority rather than to inform.

ponctuation_excessive.label: Excessive exclamation marks
ponctuation_excessive.explanation: A dense use of exclamation marks, often used to dramatize a statement rather than support it.

repetition_suspecte.label: Suspicious repetition
repetition_suspecte.explanation: The same phrase is repeated word-for-word several times in the text — a known propaganda technique ("repeat the lie") rather than a natural way of writing.

attribution_non_identifiee.label: Unnamed source
attribution_non_identifiee.explanation: The text attributes a claim to someone ("according to experts", "sources say"…) without ever naming who exactly is speaking — the source can't be verified.

metaphore_guerriere.label: War metaphor
metaphore_guerriere.explanation: The text describes a situation (migration, disease, political disagreement…) using war or invasion vocabulary — a framing technique that implicitly presents the subject as a threat to repel rather than a fact to discuss.
